clue.text: Times following up proposition Queen is not a good Samaritan?

indicators.note: following up means the piece for Times comes after the other two in the answer

parts.note: to make a pass at someone is to proposition them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
in arithmetic 'times' is BY, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Someone propositions the Queen and is then judged no Good Samaritan, a little moral tale.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable the priest and the Levite pass by on the other side; only the Samaritan stops, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from the parable: those who walked on without helping were the opposite of the Good Samaritan.

clue.text: Rather thick, putting an R in 'investigate'

indicators.note: in says the letter R is put inside the word for investigate

parts.note: to study something is to investigate it

explanation.surface: A grammar instruction: put an R into the word 'investigate', and someone thinks it's rather thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something solidly built and stout is thick-set rather than slender.

clue.text: Demand rising, business gathering cheers

indicators.note: gathering means the reversed word takes the thanks word into its middle
in a down clue rising means the word for business is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a line of business is a trade
TA is British informal for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Demand is going up, and a firm is collecting applause for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' gives ENIL before 'gathering' takes in the thanks; 'cheers' looks like applause but is British thank-you slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to necessitate or require something, as a plan that involves extra cost.

clue.text: Radiance of British justice

parts.note: rightness, being in the right, is justice

explanation.surface: A phrase praising the shining quality of British law.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: radiance is brilliance of light, a shining quality.

clue.text: Beat schoolmaster, getting time inside

indicators.note: inside says the time letter is put within the schoolmaster's title

parts.note: pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned picture of a teacher being beaten and doing time for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like corporal punishment; it is the cookery sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery synonym: to whisk or mix eggs or batter vigorously with a spoon.

clue.text: This writer involved in craftier novel, not a great

indicators.note: involved in places the writer's letter within the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not says the word a is left out of the word craftier

parts.note: the setter calling themselves this writer gives I

explanation.surface: A writer caught up in a craftier novel that is somehow not a great one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' strips A from CRAFTIER; 'novel' rearranges the rest and 'involved in' puts I among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: something excellent or wonderful is great.

clue.text: 'Bottled in Devonshire', pub licences state

indicators.note: Bottled in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A label boasting of beer bottled in Devon, with pubs holding licences to sell it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a country governed without a monarch is one kind of state or nation.

clue.text: Frenzied title boxing gave a buzz

indicators.note: boxing means the document word encloses the phoning word

parts.note: a title deed proves ownership, so deed stands in for title
to give someone a buzz is to phone them, so rang

explanation.surface: A boxing title fight that gave the crowd a thrill and had them frenzied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone wild and out of their mind is frenzied, crazed.

clue.text: Spring in France — nation rioting, university seized

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: seized means the scrambled letters take the university letter inside them
rioting suggests disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A French spring: the nation riots and a university is occupied, like Paris in 1968.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season, given the protest; it is a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a natural spring is a source of water welling up, as a fountainhead.

clue.text: Celebrity footballers on camera, taking centre

parts.note: the FA, the Football Association, governs English footballers

indicators.note: taking centre means only the middle letters of the word camera are used

explanation.surface: Footballers are filmed and take centre stage, achieving celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: celebrity as a state is renown, being widely known.

clue.text: Fitting bolster back on

parts.note: to prop something up is to bolster it

indicators.note: back means the word for on is written backwards

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting a bolster back on the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like a verb of fixing the bolster; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: appropriate or suitable, as in correct behaviour.

clue.text: Time of love, love? Love, love!

definitions.text: Time of love, love? Love, love

parts.words: Time of love, love? Love, love
parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so four loves make the twenty-four-hour clock time 00:00

explanation.surface: A romantic exclamation asking about the hour of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'love' is a nought; four noughts read as a clock time give 00:00.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the hour of twelve at night is a time on the clock.

clue.text: Oddly taking things off in train, Bob doing strip

indicators.note: removing the odd-placed letters leaves only the even ones of the words that follow

explanation.surface: On a train, a man called Bob does a striptease, oddly removing his clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'train Bob doing' and the even letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a long narrow strip of fabric, as tied in hair or on a parcel.

clue.text: They fly around stormy Polar Sea, bearing north-east

indicators.note: bearing means the scrambled letters carry the compass letters within them
stormy suggests turbulence, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Birds or planes circling a stormy Arctic sea on a north-easterly heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a compass heading but means carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: aircraft are the things that travel around through the air.

clue.text: Running hot and cold, divine liquid covers ices, melting

indicators.note: covers means the first rearranged group surrounds the second
liquid suggests flowing, so these letters are rearranged
melting means the letters of ices lose their shape and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly drink poured over melting ice, flitting between hot and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' gives INDIVE and 'melting' gives ECIS; 'covers' puts the second inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: blowing or running hot and cold means wavering, unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Gather disorder splits island where Boney was held up, …

indicators.note: in a down clue held up means the whole is read from bottom to top
splits means the disorder word breaks into the island name

parts.note: Boney is Napoleon, exiled to the island of Elba in 1814
a mess is disorder

explanation.surface: Chaos divides the island where Napoleon was confined, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' gives ELBMESSA, which 'held up' turns round; the ellipsis carries the sentence into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to collect or come together in one place.

clue.text: … captured and tied up

definitions.meaning: taken over by force, like a town held by an army
busy, engaged, with no time free

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: Napoleon on Elba, captured and bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: territory seized and held, and a person busy with something.

clue.text: Anxious struggle to get wife off ship

indicators.note: off says the wife letter is taken away

parts.note: to wrestle is to struggle
SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name

explanation.surface: A husband fighting to get his wife off a ship, which would make anyone anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unable to settle or stay still from worry or unease.

clue.text: Victory number one turned series

parts.note: a victory is a success

indicators.note: turned means the number and one pieces are written backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sporting report: a win puts the team at number one, turning the series around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sequence of things following one after another.

clue.text: One joining military force since getting over shooting expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue getting over means the whole string is turned upside down

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained'

explanation.surface: Someone who joined the army has since got over a shooting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces in order give IRAFAS, which 'getting over' turns round; 'shooting' is hunting, not filming.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition: an overland trip in Africa, traditionally to hunt big game.

clue.text: We can admire the craft in this Bernstein song about November

definitions.text: We can admire the craft in this

indicators.note: about means the song title goes around the November letter

parts.note: Maria is a song from Leonard Bernstein's West Side Story
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boast about a harbour or showroom full of boats, praised in a Bernstein song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests skill; here it means boats, moored where we can look at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a harbour for yachts and pleasure boats, where vessels are on show.

clue.text: Overcome in Lourdes, one supporting saint

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means this piece sits below the saint

parts.note: Lourdes is in France, and the French for one is un

explanation.surface: A pilgrim overcome at Lourdes, propped up beside a saint's shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to daze or overwhelm, leaving someone stupefied.

clue.text: Two Europeans having couple of pints inside run out to see match

indicators.note: inside puts the shortened measure between the two European letters

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, twice

indicators.note: out says the run letter is removed

parts.note: a quart is two pints
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Two Europeans down a couple of pints, then dash out to watch a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' removes R from QUART to leave QUAT. 'match' is the verb, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make or treat as equal, setting two things side by side.

clue.text: Agreeable rustic houses either side of Liverpool

indicators.note: houses means the country person contains the city's letter

parts.note: a rustic is a country person or peasant

indicators.note: either side of means one end letter of the city name, and both ends give the same letter

explanation.surface: A country dweller living on either side of Liverpool proves nice company.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool begins and ends in L, so 'either side' gives L whichever end you pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nice, enjoyable, pleasing to be with.

clue.text: Heated camphor used when going bye-byes, possibly?

indicators.note: going means the oil goes into the word for bye-byes

parts.note: going bye-byes is nursery talk for going to bed
camphor oil is an aromatic oil

explanation.surface: A warmed camphor rub for a child at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Nursery 'bye-byes' is sleep, hence bed; the oil goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: heated in water to boiling point, as an egg or kettle.

clue.text: Popular remix of 'So Vain' becomes offensive

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: a remix reworks a song, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A popular remix of Carly Simon's 'You're So Vain' turns out offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective about the remix; it is the noun, a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an offensive is an attack, an incursion into enemy territory.

clue.text: Sparkle — hurry — drop — shatter!

definitions.meaning: a small splash added, as of milk

explanation.surface: A frantic string of exclamations, like someone's hopes being smashed in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions: panache, rush, a small amount, and to dash hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Four senses of the one word: flair, a rush, a small splash, and to wreck.

clue.text: Likely cost of this person's cracking country pile

indicators.note: cracking means the 'I am' piece breaks into the country house

parts.note: a country estate is a grand house, informally a pile
this person's means this person is, so I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone working out what it would cost them to break into a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' suggests a burglary but just means breaking open; 'pile' is slang for a large house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quote or rough calculation of what a job will probably cost.
